Variants.Content: Moro's riders knew best that leaving the campfire of Old Kaa was both freedom and a gamble. ，；，。

Elders and caregivers in khalasar are not just about killing enemies. They looked to see if Moloch would allow the wounded horses to rest, if he would slow down the procession for the sick, and if he would admit in the distribution that the men who did not wield swords also maintained the entire camp.

The city-state envoys viewed Moloch as a force that could be negotiated but not assumed for a long time. The one who accepts the gift today is a complete khalasar, but tomorrow it may have been divided into several shares; a smart person will not only talk about Kaa, but also recognize the most important Kou around him.
